quote: Ist [-xx-] Existenz solcher anderen Substitutionen wirklich von Nöther Math. Ann. [-xx-] Bd. 3. S. 547 letzter § bewiesen?
english: Is the existence of such other substitutions really proved by Nöther, Math. Ann. vol. 3, p. 547, last section?
topic: Notes on reducing birational (Cremona) transformations of the plane to quadratic or linear ones, a question about such transformations in space with a reference to Nöther in Math. Ann. Bd. 3, and the start of a proof that a series of continuous functions converging continuously on an interval converges uniformly.

triage.modern_statement: Hilbert is asking whether Noether really proved, in Math. Ann. 3 (1871), pp. 547–580, last section, that space has birational (Cremona) transformations that cannot be built from the simple ones. In modern terms: in dimension 3 and higher, is the Cremona group Bir(P^n) strictly larger than the subgroup generated by the linear maps PGL_{n+1} together with the standard involution (or other simple maps of low degree)? In the plane the answer is no: by the Noether–Castelnuovo theorem these maps generate everything. I am inferring what Noether's last section says from the page context and the paper's title. I have not read the section itself.
triage.answered_by: Modern Cremona-group theory settles the question. Blanc and Hedén (Ann. Inst. Fourier 65 (2015), arXiv:1405.2746) showed that every element of the group generated by PGL_{n+1} and the standard involution contracts only rational hypersurfaces. Since Bir(P^n) for n≥3 contains maps that contract non-rational hypersurfaces, these 'other substitutions' do exist. Blanc, Lamy and Zimmermann (Acta Math. 226 (2021)) went further: over subfields of C, Cr_n for n≥3 is not simple and has many non-trivial quotients. Earlier work (H. Hudson 1927; I. Pan, 1999) is usually credited with the first results that Cr_3 cannot be generated by maps of bounded degree, but my searches did not reach those sources, so I cite only the papers I could check.

evidence.claim: Noether's paper 'Ueber die eindeutigen Raumtransformationen, insbesondere in ihrer Anwendung auf die Abbildung algebraischer Flächen' appeared in Math. Ann. vol. 3, pp. 547–580 (1871). This is the reference in Hilbert's note.
In the plane, Cr_2 is generated by PGL_3 and the standard quadratic involution (Noether–Castelnuovo). This is the plane case of the reduction Hilbert discusses.

Blanc and Hedén study the group generated by PGL_{n+1} and the standard involution of degree n. Every element of it contracts only rational hypersurfaces, so it is a proper subgroup of the Cremona group in higher dimensions.
Blanc, Lamy and Zimmermann proved that over subfields of C, Cr_n is not simple for n≥3 and has many non-trivial quotients.
A later paper on Cremona maps of P^4 describes the higher-dimensional Cremona groups as large and rigid. This shows the area is still studied.

triage.why: The reference matches exactly: Noether's 1871 paper on space transformations starts on p. 547 of Math. Ann. 3. On the page, the note follows Hilbert's remarks on reducing plane Cremona maps to quadratic and linear ones. The natural reading is whether space really has transformations that do not reduce in this way, unlike the plane. Modern results confirm such transformations exist: the group generated by linear maps and the standard involution is a proper subgroup of Bir(P^n) for n≥3, and the higher Cremona groups have rich quotients. This is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th. Confidence is medium for two reasons. I could not read Noether's last section, so I cannot say exactly what it claims or whether its proof was complete. My searches also did not reach the classical sources (Hudson, Pan) usually credited with the first rigorous results.
